name: Buddy Holly glasses

image.caption: Buddys Glasses 1, Buddy Holly Center, Lubbock, TX

lead: Buddy Holly glasses are thick, dark, rectangular frames named after the 1950s rock and roll singer. They add a strong horizontal line across the face, framing the eyes and brows and giving a retro, bookish look.
The style came from Holly's own frames, which he got from a Lubbock optometrist and which teenagers then asked for by name. It has been revived by later musicians and fashion trends.

paras: Wearers choose a heavy acetate or similar frame in black, tortoiseshell or another dark colour, usually paired with vintage-leaning clothes such as cardigans and collared shirts. Fit matters: width relative to the face and brow position change how the frame reads.
Eyewear carries no meaningful health risk beyond fit and prescription accuracy. Style opinion varies; some online posters mock the look as hipster, while others wear it deliberately.

lead: Buddy Holly glasses are heavy, rectangular horn-rimmed frames named for the singer Buddy Holly. Wearers use them to add structure around the eyes and to signal a retro or studious style. [1][2]

According to Wikipedia, the Everly Brothers advised Holly to swap his old-fashioned glasses for horn-rimmed frames, a look Steve Allen had popularized, and Holly bought Mexican-made frames from Lubbock optometrist Dr. J. Davis Armistead. American teenagers then began asking for the style. [2] A 2007 Canadian Journal of Ophthalmology article based on correspondence with Armistead describes the glasses as part of Holly's performing identity. [1]
The look was later echoed by others, including Steve Marriott, who wore large-rimmed spectacles with the lenses removed, and Elvis Costello during punk. [2]

paras: The frames are thick, dark and rectangular with a defined brow line, in the horn-rimmed tradition. [2]

Holly's glasses came from his optometrist in Lubbock; the ophthalmology journal piece recounts the story from the prescriber himself. [1] Wikipedia reports that after Holly's death the glasses went missing until a sheriff found them in storage in 1980, and they are now at the Buddy Holly Center in Lubbock. [2]
A 2010 T Nation thread on hipsters shows the frames being used as shorthand for hipster style, with one poster disparaging it. [3]
